research_question: Does a short reference ECG at the start of each monitoring session calibrate the record-varying timing and amplitude of continuous radar-to-ECG reconstruction?
motivation: The preregistered one-record subject calibration failed on 2/3 subjects, showing that one fixed subject constant does not transfer across records. This separate probe tests session calibration rather than changing that failed result.
output: Full-window continuous ECG, 1600 samples at 200 Hz

calibration_protocol.guard: no calibration and query window shares an ECG or radar sample
calibration_protocol.inference: one lag and affine map are stored per session; query receives radar plus those stored constants

lag_search: integer samples in [-40,40] selected on calibration prefix only
metrics: query-only per-window full-1600 PCC/RMSE/MAE/R2; subject/fold summaries retain record-level counts

gate.required: lag_affine improves all 3 subjects, mean delta PCC >= 0.15, and at least 80% of records improve
gate.on_fail: calibration alone is not a sufficient main method
